description: A single-panel multi-axis property chart (no lettered sub-panels) comparing four mechanical quantities across eleven austenitizing (T_A) / austempering (T_B) conditions of the Al–C steels S1–S5. The categorical x-axis carries 90°-rotated labels such as "S1, T_A: 1150 °C, T_B: 350 °C", "S1, T_A: 1150 °C, T_B: 300 °C", "S3, T_A: 1220 °C, T_B: 270 °C", "S4, T_A: 1250 °C, T_B: 350 °C", "S5, T_A: 1150 °C, T_B: 365 °C" and "S5, T_A: 1150 °C, T_B: 335 °C". Three vertical scales coexist: a black left axis UTS (MPa) 200–2000 with gridlines every 200; a blue right axis Rpo.2 (MPa) 800–1400 (step 100); and a red right axis El (%) with even ticks up to 12. A further red tick row along the top edge (values ~100–1400) has no legible quantity label. Legend, printed exactly: "UTS (MPa)" black squares, "El (%)" red up-triangles, "Rpo.2 (MPa)" blue down-triangles, "Hardness (HV30)" black circles. Every marker carries a vertical error bar. Hardness values are printed at each black circle left to right: 464, 497, 465, 500, 443, 457, 464, 479, 467, 459, 493. UTS and Rp0.2 are highest for the S1/S2 columns austempered at 300 °C (near the 1600 MPa gridline and the top of the blue scale), while the tallest red El triangle is the S4, T_A 1150 °C, T_B 350 °C column — the low-alloy S4/S5 conditions keep comparable strength and hardness but give the best elongation.

observations.observation: The group is one single multi-axis scatter/error-bar chart with no lettered sub-panels; four mechanical quantities are compared over eleven steel/heat-treatment conditions.
The printed legend entries are 'UTS (MPa)' (black squares), 'El (%)' (red up-triangles), 'Rpo.2 (MPa)' (blue down-triangles, spelled 'Rpo.2') and 'Hardness (HV30)' (black circles).
The left black y-axis is labelled 'UTS (MPa)' and runs from 200 to 2000 with gridlines every 200 MPa.
A blue right-hand axis is labelled 'Rpo.2 (MPa)' and spans 800–1400 in steps of 100; a red right-hand axis carries even ticks up to 12 for El (%).

A red tick row along the top edge of the plot (values from about 100 to 1400) carries no legible quantity label; linking it to the 'Hardness (HV30)' legend entry is an inference, not something printed.
Every marker of all four series has a vertical error bar; the bars on El (red) and Rpo.2 (blue) are the largest, sometimes spanning several gridline intervals.
Hardness (HV30) values are printed beside the black circles, left to right: 464, 497, 465, 500, 443, 457, 464, 479, 467, 459, 493.

The highest UTS markers reach approximately the 1600 MPa gridline in the S1 and S2 columns austempered at T_B = 300 °C; those same columns show the highest Rpo.2, near the top of the 800–1400 blue scale.
Red El triangles sit mostly between the 6 and 10 positions of the red scale; the tallest one is in the column labelled 'S4, T_A: 1150 °C, T_B: 350 °C'.
Black UTS squares cluster between roughly the 1300 and 1600 MPa gridlines, i.e. no condition shifts UTS by more than about two gridline steps.
The rotated x-axis labels name five steels (S1, S2, S3, S4, S5) with T_A of 1150, 1220 or 1250 °C and T_B of 270, 300, 320, 335, 350 or 365 °C.
The caption states that the figure presents UTS (MPa), R_p0.2 (MPa), El (%) and hardness (HV30) of the investigated steels under various austenitization (T_A) and austempering (T_B) conditions.
The citing text states that the S4 steel exhibited the best average and maximum El of 10 and 12 % at T_A 1150 °C and T_B 350 °C, slightly higher than S1 and S2 (see Fig. 7).
The citing text states that the lower alloying concept suppresses variation of the bainite thickness distribution Lt(t), which is regarded as an El-improving factor as shown in Fig. 7.

unreadable_items: Top-edge red tick row: quantity label missing/unreadable, so which series it scales (presumably Hardness (HV30)) cannot be confirmed from the image
No numeric data labels are printed for UTS, Rpo.2 or El points — only gridline positions can be read
Exact T_B values of the middle columns (read as 270, 300, 320, 350 °C from small rotated labels) are only partially legible
Error-bar magnitudes are not numerically annotated
